uncited: Spatial Hierarchies organize volumetric or geometric data into a tree structure to accelerate ray traversal by skipping empty space and reducing intersection tests.
Unlike flat voxel grids, they adapt resolution to data density, solving the problem of inefficient sampling in sparse volumes.

They differ from sibling methods like [Hierarchical Spatial Enumeration Optimization](1663-hierarchical-spatial-enumeration-optimization.md) by relying on explicit geometric bounding volumes rather than spatial enumeration indices, and from [Jiang et al. Acceleration Structure](1673-jiang-et-al-acceleration-structure.md) by using recursive subdivision rather than specific silhouette-based pruning.
The traversal begins at the root of the octree and determines which of the eight children (octants) the ray intersects.
They are widely used in computer graphics for rendering complex scenes and volumes.
